analysis: Both supplied units are CHANGELOG.md text excerpts (head side, lines ~418-611+). They are documentation only; no executable code, configuration, or mode/rename changes were supplied. The changelog describes security-relevant behavior: App Attest dead-key rotation (limits of one per machine per hour and four per 24h, and a 6h backoff after three invalidKey failures), untrusted ready-reply diagnostics outside the signed transcript, qualified App Attest serving authorization alongside legacy MDM/APNs, per-handoff authorization fencing, durable build qualification and revocation, and unenrollment gating. These statements are consistent with the canonical threat model entries (TB-002 on untrusted diagnostics that never grant, extend or revoke authorization; TB-009; TB-011; T-052..T-058). The changelog states that rotation 'never revoke[s] or deny[s] serving' and that rotated keys must pass the full attestation, receipt, build-qualification and assertion checks, so no invalidated assumption is visible from the text. The implementing source for the rotation (admission serialization with machine merges, EIGENINFERENCE_APP_ATTEST_KEY_ROTATION_PERCENT default 100, key-rotation budget carryover), coordinator/appattest/service/ready_diagnostics.go, and the APNs retry paths was not supplied. A later pass should verify those code paths. In particular, check that rotation cannot be used to evade revocation or credential denial (T-053, T-055), that rotated keys inherit revocation state, and that forged diagnostics (e.g. launch_session, operation_stalled_seconds) cannot influence authorization or the self-restart behavior. No security finding is raised from the changelog alone; this reflects a coverage limit and not a clearance of the underlying code.
